parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Mehtab Khan, Moinudeen Khan, Shakoor Khan (all s/o Sh.Bhure Khan)

facts_of_case: Complainant's Firm allotted industrial plot. Complainant took help of one Shaukat Khan and rented the plot. After Shaukat Khan expired, complainant came to know that the name of the Firm has been changed to 'Nasrani Steel', and the land had been usurped by means of a forged partnership deed.

legal_principles.principle: Abuse of process of law can be quashed if the parties have entered into a compromise and the criminal complaint is no longer surviving against the present petitioner.
legal_principles.held: Counsel for the petitioner has further pointed out from the agreement in which condition No.8 clearly stipulate the withdrawal of the present criminal proceedings.
cited_cases: Ruchi Agarwal Vs. Amit Kumar Agrawal & Ors., (2005) Supreme Court Cases (Cri) 719

legal_principles.principle: A compromise agreement can be used to withdraw criminal proceedings if the parties have agreed to do so.
legal_principles.held: In the compromise petition, referred to herein above, both the parties had agreed to withdraw all the civil and criminal cases filed by each against the other.
cited_cases: Ruchi Agarwal Vs. Amit Kumar Agrawal & Ors., (2005) Supreme Court Cases (Cri) 719

outcome.final_order: FIR No.456/2012 dated 12.12.2012 registered at Police Station, Udaimandir, Jodhpur and all consequential proceedings quashed.

use_for_drafting: responding to complaint under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
